description: GasDispersion.jl is a Julia package for estimating the spread of a gas released into the atmosphere. It provides plume and puff formulations with worked examples that calculate concentration at a specified downwind position and height. Inputs are release rate, wind and atmospheric conditions, source geometry and receptor coordinates; outputs are concentration estimates over a chosen place and period. Its spatial and temporal coverage is the user-defined accident or industrial source, not a mapped national network. MIT-licensed source and documentation are free on GitHub and through Julia's package system. A limitation is that simplified dispersion formulas rely on their meteorological and terrain assumptions and do not represent all urban flow or chemical reactions. Results should not be treated as measured exposure. The model can support hazardous-material transport, pipeline and industrial emergency-planning simulations. The catalogue's model-aloha-chemical-dispersion is a related emergency-release tool for comparison, not a dependency. No release scenario was run.
